scope: Set the reference architecture baseline for the HR Copilot across three explicit sub-decisions: agent orchestration and tool execution; AI model and policy retrieval; and ticket/audit versus conversation-state persistence. The baseline is the user-supplied Azure design, not an implementation or deployment approval.

drivers.statement: Preserve tenant-, role-, ownership-, and direct-report authorization while preventing disclosure of medical and compensation data.
drivers.evidence: SOP-HR-042 sections 6.1-6.2; PRD NFR-005 through NFR-010

drivers.statement: Keep human accountability for approvals, explicit ticket lifecycle state, reliable SLA processing, and attributable audit records.
drivers.evidence: SOP-HR-042 sections 5.2 and 7.2; SPEC-HRIS-014; PRD FR-003 and FR-004

drivers.statement: Meet the user-facing response-time and service availability targets without losing ticket or SLA events.
Support policy-grounded responses and replaceable HRIS/ERP integration boundaries while controlling Azure model, search, compute, and storage costs.
drivers.evidence: User-supplied architecture blueprint; PRD NFR-011 and NFR-015; Marketplace Lean Canvas

constraints: The evidence is synthetic workshop material and is not a verified production policy, live tenant configuration, or legal determination.
Human managers or authorized HR administrators make ticket decisions; the agent must not self-approve, self-reject, or impersonate a user.
Medical details and compensation-sensitive values must be minimized and withheld from unauthorized roles, Teams cards, model transcripts, and general-purpose logs.
Every lifecycle action requires an attributable, append-only or tamper-evident audit record.

The user-supplied baseline includes Teams, Entra ID OBO, Azure App Service with LangGraph and internal MCP, Foundry, Azure AI Search, Storage, separate Cosmos DB stores, HRIS/Graph connectors, Service Bus, and Functions.

The SLA evidence conflicts: SOP-HR-042 describes a 48-business-hour reminder and escalation after 72 hours, while SPEC-HRIS-014 shows escalation after a 48-hour SLA. Timer semantics must be confirmed before implementation.

decisionOptions.evaluationProvenance: Alternatives and rejection reasons reported by the user as having been evaluated by the architecture group; not independently verified.

options.name: LangGraph state machine and MCP tools in Azure App Service
pros: Supports inspectable ticket workflow state and human pause/resume at manager approval.
MCP provides a standardized boundary for pluggable HRIS and enterprise tools.
cons: Requires operating and securing the orchestration service, MCP server, and connector contracts.

options.name: Stateless prompt chaining or OpenAI Assistants API
pros: Can reduce the amount of custom workflow orchestration for simple conversational tasks.
cons: Does not provide the required deterministic, inspectable ticket state machine and manager approval pause/resume.

options.name: Proprietary custom REST connector per HRIS
pros: Can map directly to one selected HRIS API and its vendor-specific operations.
cons: Tightly couples the agent to vendor-specific APIs and undermines the requested portable connector boundary.

decisionOptions.evaluationProvenance: Alternatives and rejection reasons reported by the user as having been evaluated by the architecture group; not independently verified.

options.name: Azure AI Foundry with hybrid BM25/vector Azure AI Search and semantic reranking
pros: Combines exact-term and policy-code retrieval with semantic matching and reranking for cited answers.
cons: Adds index, semantic-ranker, and model cost and requires retrieval-quality and latency evaluation.

options.name: Dense vector-only search
pros: Provides a simpler semantic retrieval path with fewer retrieval modes to tune.
cons: Can miss exact numeric values and policy codes or return semantically similar but incorrect clauses.

options.name: Full-context policy window stuffing
pros: Avoids building and operating a separate retrieval index for smaller policy collections.
cons: Increases token consumption and latency as the policy library grows, conflicting with the p95 target.

decisionOptions.evaluationProvenance: Alternatives and rejection reasons reported by the user as having been evaluated by the architecture group; not independently verified.

options.name: Separate Cosmos DB stores for tickets/audit and conversation memory
pros: Creates distinct access, retention, and lifecycle boundaries for workflow records and short-lived conversation state.
cons: Requires explicit cross-store consistency and recovery design; Cosmos DB alone does not provide immutable audit guarantees.

options.name: One unified Azure SQL database
pros: Provides relational constraints and transaction support for structured ticket operations.
cons: The reported design concern is retention and schema coupling between ticket/audit records and conversation memory; separate schemas and tables could mitigate but not remove all governance coupling.

options.name: Tickets stored directly as Azure Blob files
pros: Provides low-cost durable object storage for documents and archival payloads.
cons: Is not a suitable sole system of record for transactional updates, concurrency control, and manager-indexed pending-ticket queries.
